blocks.x: Underwriting evidence assembled in hours — case cycle time down 44%
A leading life insurer (North America) — Insurance & Risk engagement delivered by a 16-person team over 12 months, US/Canada scope, commercial model: build-transfer.

items: APS records and paramedical data arrived as faxes and PDFs; evidence assembly took 9 days average per case.
Underwriting health data spread across systems with inconsistent access control.
Lapse signals arrived too late for retention action.

blocks.x: KYC Management System agents classify, extract and assemble underwriting evidence with confidence routing; the actuarial data workbench on Forge unified valuation and experience pipelines with lineage for LDTI reporting; sensitive health data moved under classification-aware controls. Lapse models now trigger retention actions within weeks of drift signals.

Programs stall when the operating model is an afterthought: no named owner for the seam, no eval gate on changes, no rollback rehearsed before launch. The failure is organizational before it is technical.

items: Engineered for Insurance & Risk from day one: contracts first, runbooks shipped with the working slice
Target range down 52 on the first working slice, with the method note attached

blocks.x: Towers: Agentic AI & Hyperautomation, Data, Analytics & Lakehouse, Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust. Platforms: KYC Management System, Fleet Management System.

items: What moved unchanged between sectors, and why it was safe to move — stated plainly.
What does not transfer between estates, and the adaptation it needs — named before the pilot, not after.

blocks.x: The engagement's evidence trail is available to your auditors under NDA — the same standard every Achala program carries.
See the method behind this case at a briefing: the measurement, the gates and the evidence your auditors would ask for.
